why: The host entry surface as shape classes, and the entry names that reach each one.
A shape is the call a caller meets, not the name it is spelled with: a run-time route, a
route-named sibling, a sorted-argument overload and a span overload are spellings of one
shape, so a table of shapes does not grow every time an alias is added.
The axes a shape offers are derived from its tuple by check_host_entry_bijection.py and are
not written here: a one-order shape has no ladder to fill a packed register with, so its
packing axis is a single default by construction rather than by a refusal in this file.
Read by tools/check_host_entry_bijection.py, which holds this table to the headers in both
directions. Edit it when an entry moves between shapes; the check names what it cannot place.

shapes.evidence: BoysSingle(n, x) returns F_n(x) by value: one order, one argument, no array.
BoysDouble(n, x, out) returns an int status and writes *out: the C surface.
BoysAllOrders(nmax, x, out): F_0..F_nmax of one argument, the top named once.
BoysFixedN(n, x, out, count, stride): one fixed order at each argument.
BoysAllN(nmax, x, out, count): order-major planes, out[k*count+i], one nmax.
BoysAllNAtOrders(n, x, out, count): each column stops at its own n[i].
BoysDoubleBatch(nmax, count, x, out): the plane shape behind a status.
BoysDoubleBatchAtOrders(n, count, x, out): per-element tops, behind a status.

not_an_evaluation.BoysEvalSchemeDelivered: one figure read from those rows

not_an_evaluation.FitGranularityHasAxis: a bit test on a partition row's axis mask

not_an_evaluation.BoysAccuracyDelivered: the figure a combination's rows were measured to deliver
not_an_evaluation.GuaranteeAxesAreEnumerators: a constexpr test on whether seven axis cells are inside their enumerations, the refusal BoysAccuracyGuaranteed makes at run time
